newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gonzalez cautious on Serbia poll reversal.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gonzalez cautious on Serbia poll reversal.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez reacted cautiously to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's move to reinstate opposition election victories as Gonzalez had recommended in a report on behalf of the OSCE.
Milosevic conceded the opposition victories in 14 towns and cities after 78 days of street protests against his earlier decision to annul results of November municipal elections.

Gonzalez visited Serbia in December as special envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to study the disputed polls. He then issued a report which recommended the government accept opposition election victories.

The report also recommended the government open a dialogue with the opposition about the country's move to democracy and specifically on media freedom, independence of the courts and the electoral process.
"We can only congratulate ourselves if they (the report's recommendations) are fulfilled," Gonzalez said in an interview with Spanish radio on Wednesday night.
Milosevic cited the OSCE findings as a factor in his decision to recognise the opposition victories.
